in_sanskrit.name: उज्जवल

in_telugu.name: ఉజ్జ్వళ్

in_marathi.name: Ujjaval

data.cultural_impact: The name Ujjaval, derived from the Sanskrit word "ujjvala" meaning "brilliant, radiant, burning," suggests someone who excels in various fields, particularly in the acquisition and dissemination of knowledge. In Hindu culture, education and wisdom are highly respected virtues. The name implies the bearer is a spiritual scholar, a wise sage, or a revered guru.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ujjaval carries deep spiritual significance, suggesting an enlightened self, one who is cognizant of the infinite wisdom inherent in the universe. It implies the individual has gained the inner light of knowledge through dedicated spiritual practice and has come to realize the unity of all things in the divine consciousness. Thus, Ujjaval represents the pursuit of wisdom and knowledge as a means of obtaining inner peace, self-realization, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Ujjayin, the ancient capital of the Avanti Mahajanpada, was ruled by the Sisunaka dynasty during the 5th century BCE. The renowned king Ujjval is believed to have reigned during this time. He is known for his patronage of Jain scholarship and for his piety towards both Jain and Buddhist monks.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Avanti Mahajanpada, Sisunaka dynasty, King Ujjval, Jain scholarship, Buddhist monks

historical_references.reference: Ujjain was an important cultural and religious centre in medieval India. The city was ruled by the Kalachuris from the 10th to the 13th centuries CE. King Ujjvaldeva, a notable monarch during this period, is believed to have built several temples, including the Mahakaleshwar temple, that are still revered in the region.
historical_references.context: Medieval India, Ujjain, Kalachuris, King Ujjvaldeva, Mahakaleshwar temple
